newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-PARNEVIK CLINGS TO LEAD OVER LEONARD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK CLINGS TO LEAD OVER LEONARD.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik of Sweden, trying to atone for blowing the 1994 title, led red-hot American Justin Leonard by just two shots with nine holes left in the British Open on Sunday.
Northern Irishman Darren Clarke was another shot behind but Tiger Woods blew his chances with a triple bogey six at the Postage Stamp eighth, at 126 yards the shortest hole in the British Open rota.

The eccentric Parnevik, sartorially inelegant in purple drainpipe trousers, survived a shaky front nine that included a bogey six at the 577-yard, but often birdied, sixth hole to go with birdies at the third and seventh holes.

Leonard, the fast-rising 26-year-old American, birdied the second, third and fourth, dropped a shot at the fifth, then added birdies at three of the next four holes for an outward nine-under-par half of 31.
Then, having got within a shot of the lead, he dropped one at the 10th to slip back to two behind.
Clarke birdied the first but hit out of bounds with the iron shot he selected for safety off the second tee and took a double bogey six.
Both Parnevik, wearing his trademark cap with an upturned brim, and Clarke hit the pin with their approaches at the third, but where Parnevik birdied, Clarke missed from four feet and took par.
He birdied the sixth but dropped one at the ninth when his approach found heavy rough.
U.S. Masters champion Woods failed to get the fast start he needed to cut back his eight-shot overnight deficit as he could only par the first three holes.
Birdies at the fourth and fifth hinted at a recovery but it all went wrong for the 21-year-old American at the short eighth.
The world number one struck his tee shot into a deep pot bunker and took two to get out, then from 18 feet ran his putt four feet past and missed it.
Playing four groups in front of the leaders, he then missed a two-footer at the 12th.
Earlier Parnevik hit an iron off the first tee and still had 150 yards to go but pulled his second shot into a greenside bunker in a downhill lie.
But he blasted out to 18 inches and holed to save par, then made a routine par at the second.
American Tom Lehman ended his disappointing title defence on an upbeat note with a five-under-par 66 containing five birdies and no dropped shots.
"I played awfully well last week to win at Loch Lomond but I didn't have my game this week.
"The back nine has kicked me in the butt all week and my two birdies on the back nine today were my first all week," he said.
Triple winner Nick Faldo completed what seemed likely to be his worst British Open since he was joint 53rd in 1985.
Faldo, the winner in 1987, 1990 and 1992, compiled a closing 72 after birdies at the last two holes for a total of 291, seven over par.
He was unlikely to make the top 50.
"My game was about 10 percent off this week and that makes a big difference. You have to keep the ball in play and I was not in play the whole time," he said.
Another three-times champion, Jack Nicklaus, finished with a 75 for 293, nine over par.
